reason: While the text includes worship elements (altars, sacrifices, theophanic manifestations), it emphasizes that Israel becomes God's special people through covenant acceptance and obedience to God's commandments—not worship per se. Exodus 19:5-6 explicitly states they will be God's 'special treasure' (סְגוּלָה) and 'kingdom of priests and holy nation' IF they 'listen to His voice and keep His covenant.' The defining relationship is covenant commitment and law observance. The golden calf incident (Exodus 32) further illustrates this: the people engage in worship practices (building an altar, offering sacrifices) yet are severely punished because they violated the covenant itself. The text consistently prioritizes covenantal fidelity and legal observance over worship as constitutive of their identity as a people.
